verified.title: G5 identifiability+anisotropy trigger is frozen with zero positive calibration and measures menu distinctness, not privilege
verified.claim: The PRIV-1 arm of G5 (accuracy > IDENT_ACC_HI jointly with aniso > ANISO_HI) has never fired on any synthetic control, its planned frozen thresholds (0.35/0.85 via anti_cheat/freeze.py) sit above the accuracy attained by BOTH calibration poles, and on real substrates it will classify the designer's own operator menu back onto itself: any menu of five mechanically distinct operators (bitflip vs rotation vs block ops) is identifiable from displacement regardless of corridor structure.
verified.evidence: C3_CORRIDOR_results.json: identifiability accuracy 0.2624 (chance 0.2467) — the CORRIDOR pole scores at chance because op4 is rarity-suppressed (60/2470 test rows, recall 1.0); C3's PRIVILEGED_CORRIDOR came solely from the ablation arm (drop 1.0, z=6.48). C5: acc 0.2010 (chance 0.200). So across all validation the trigger's firing region was never entered. Worse: in 6 of 7 controls mutate() never reads op_index (synthetic.py — C1, C2, C4, C5, C6, C7 all ignore it), so PRIV-1 labels carry zero information by construction everywhere except C3's one rare op; there is no heterogeneous-but-fair pole anywhere in the validation set. Meanwhile the accuracy gate is ABSOLUTE (gates.py: ident_res['accuracy'] > th['IDENT_ACC_HI']) while chance is data-dependent class-imbalance (majority share, classifier.py) — exposure conflated with competence. And ANISO_HI was calibrated on synthetic disp_features built from SIGNED coordinate deltas (synthetic.py FEAT_DIM comment), while VM disp_features (vm_substrates.py) are NON-NEGATIVE per-probe mismatch fractions with out[0]=d1 being exactly the mean of out[2:10] — a built-in linear dependence plus a magnitude 'size factor' that generically inflates the top covariance eigenshare on real substrates. A navigation-passing VM substrate can plausibly clear both arms and be killed PRIVILEGED_CORRIDOR for having a distinguishable menu — the predecessor's tautology inverted: the neutrality gate relabelled the menu as neutral; this privilege gate relabels menu distinctness as privilege.
verified.suggested_fix: Before freeze: (a) demote the identifiability+anisotropy trigger to diagnostics-only (report acc, chance, confusion, aniso; never gate), OR (b) add two controls — a heterogeneous-fair pole (5 distinct step kernels, all reaching everywhere; must NOT fire) and a common-directional-partitioning pole (must fire) — gate on accuracy RELATIVE to reported chance, remove the redundant d1 coordinate (or standardize features before the covariance), and re-validate all controls with the final thresholds.
verified.verify_reasoning: Every load-bearing element of the claim checks out against the actual files. (1) Zero positive calibration: the G5 joint trigger (acc>IDENT_ACC_HI AND aniso>ANISO_HI) never fired on any of the seven controls — C3_CORRIDOR_results.json shows acc 0.2624 (chance 0.2467, op4 rarity-suppressed at 60 of 3,952 test rows with recall 1.0) and its PRIVILEGED_CORRIDOR verdict came solely from the ablation arm (rel_drop 1.0, z=6.48); C5 shows acc 0.2010 (chance 0.200), aniso 0.412. (2) anti_cheat/freeze.py rewrites gates.py thresholds to 0.35/0.85 at freeze; both calibration poles' accuracies (0.201, 0.262) sit below 0.35, so the accuracy cut is bracketed from below only — the joint firing region contains no validated exemplar, positive or negative-but-heterogeneous. (3) In d4core/synthetic.py, mutate() ignores op_index in C1, C2, C4, C5, C6, C7 (only C3 reads it), and C5's five operators are identical distributions — so PRIV-1 labels carry zero information by construction everywhere except C3's one rare op, and no heterogeneous-but-fair control exists to bound false fires against exactly the real substrates' configuration (five mechanically distinct kernels in vm_substrates.py: bitflip/substitution/block-copy/block-swap/rotation, which plausibly separate on displacement magnitude alone regardless of corridor structure). (4) gates.py gates on absolute accuracy (ident_res['accuracy'] > th['IDENT_ACC_HI']) while classifier.py's chance is the data-dependent majority-class share of non-identity rows, reported only in margins — differential per-op identity rates on real substrates will skew class shares, conflating exposure with competence. (5) The feature-geometry mismatch is real: synthetic disp_features (FEAT_DIM=12) use SIGNED coordinate deltas; VM disp_features (13-dim) are all non-negative per-probe mismatch fractions with out[0]=d1 exactly equal to mean(out[2:10]) — an exact built-in linear dependence plus a common magnitude factor — and metrics.py computes anisotropy on the RAW unstandardized covariance, so the 0.85 threshold was calibrated on a feature family the real substrates never produce. I deliberately did not run the real VM op census to test the aniso prediction, since the constitution forbids real-substrate measurement before freeze; but the defect does not hinge on that number: either the arm can fire on real substrates in a region never validated (false-kill of a fair, navigation-passing substrate as PRIVILEGED_CORRIDOR — the P3-failure FATAL verdict, unrepairable after freeze), or it can never fire and is a vacuous gate violating the prereg's own attainability discipline (PREREG-INSTRUMENT §9). The prereg does not already handle this: the G5 parenthetical in PREREG-PHASE1 §10 discloses the calibration values and asserts the trigger 'targets common+directional menu partitioning', but no control demonstrates either that it fires on such partitioning or that it stays silent on a fair-but-distinct menu — an unvalidated assertion inside a kill gate, the predecessor's tautological menu-classification defect inverted. Minor immaterial errors in the claim: test-row denominator quoted as 2,470 (actual 3,952), and 'will classify' overstates what is more precisely an unbounded, plausible risk. verified.title: No floor separates target strata from the hit criterion: navigation gates are satisfiable at the start sample, and the new inclusive-band edit makes full degeneracy silent
verified.claim: Nothing constrains near/mid/far remoteness relative to EPS_HIT=0.10 or to the ab-initio start distribution, and every navigator counts a hit scored on the very first _sample_viable_start draw; so G4's pooled-hit arm (both pair navigators >= 0.25) and G6's refind can be satisfied by ab-initio adjacency with zero navigation, and under tied remoteness distributions the 'far' stratum silently ceases to be far — a by-construction path to a false PASS.
verified.evidence: Empirically confirmed on the corridor control: C3_CORRIDOR_results.json targets_meta shows near remoteness 0.079-0.081 < EPS_HIT 0.10 (an AVERAGE random start is inside the hit ball) and mid 0.107-0.112 barely outside; near hit rates: N1 1.000, N3 0.917, N2/N4 1.000 — 12 of 18 targets trivially reached, so the pooled 0.25 arm was carried by start-adjacency, not navigation. navigators.py: n1/n2/n3/n4 all return hit immediately after the start sample (e.g., n2: 'd_cur = sub.d1m(f, target_fp); if d_cur <= eps_hit: return _mk_result(True, ...)'). The 2026-08-27 live edit to select_targets (inclusive bands '>= q[1]', '>= q[3]' + chosen_global dedup, comment 'strict inequalities could leave a stratum empty') means that when remoteness ties collapse the quantiles (q[0]==q[3]), 'far' targets are drawn from the SAME tied remoteness value as 'near' with no POOL_DEGENERATE flag — MIN_FAR_HIT then gates on targets that are not far, and the substrate can pass G4 entirely without navigation. There is no N1-floor comparison anywhere in the gates to distinguish navigation from restart-lottery/start-adjacency.
verified.suggested_fix: Preregister before freeze: (1) a stratum-separation gate, e.g. far median remoteness >= near median + 2*EPS_HIT and near-stratum remoteness > EPS_HIT, else emit a degenerate-strata status that blocks PASS (report it as a physics fact, not an instrument error); (2) exclude start-sample hits (evals_to_hit == start cost) from gated hit rates, or report 'navigated hits' separately and gate on those; (3) report N1's rates beside the pair as the sampling floor.
verified.verify_reasoning:
Every load-bearing element of the claim checks out against the actual files, and no part of the preregistration handles it.

1. No floor separates strata from the hit criterion. In F:/prometheus/agent_d4_blind/d4core/metrics.py select_targets(), strata are pure quantiles of the pool's own remoteness distribution (q = np.quantile(remoteness, [0.10, 0.45, 0.55, 0.90])); nothing anywhere compares any stratum's remoteness to EPS_HIT=0.10 or to the ab-initio start distribution. gates.py never sees remoteness at all. Grep confirms: no POOL_DEGENERATE/separation check exists, gates.py contains no reference to N1 and no use of evals_to_hit — there is no navigation-vs-start-adjacency discriminator in any gated quantity.

2. Start-sample hits count. All four navigators in navigators.py return hit=True immediately after _sample_viable_start (n1/n2/n3 check right after the start draw; n4 checks during population init; n2's quoted line 'd_cur = sub.d1m(f, target_fp); if d_cur <= eps_hit: return _mk_result(True, ...)' is verbatim). N2 also re-checks at every restart (~20 fresh ab-initio draws per 1200-eval run), so gated hit rates include a restart lottery with zero navigation.

3. Empirical evidence verified exactly on C3_CORRIDOR_results.json: near remoteness 0.0791–0.0812 (< EPS_HIT 0.10, i.e., the AVERAGE random start is inside the hit ball), mid 0.1067–0.1124; near hit rates N1 18/18=1.000, N3 11/12=0.917, N2 30/30, N4 30/30; all 30 N2 near hits have evals_to_hit=1 (the start sample itself); 133 of 240 total C3 hits at evals_to_hit<=5. So 12 of 18 targets were trivially reached and the pooled arm (near+mid = 2/3 of runs > 0.25 threshold) is satisfiable entirely by start-adjacency. G6's refind_ratio is a mean over once-hit targets of per-seed hit fractions, so trivially-adjacent targets (per-seed fraction ~1.0) carry it the same way.

4. The inclusive-band edit is real, live, and uncommitted (git diff HEAD shows '>' -> '>=' on mid/far masks + chosen_global dedup, dated in the working tree 2026-08-27). I simulated it: under fully tied remoteness q[0]==q[3], the live code emits status "OK" with 8 'far' targets drawn from the SAME tied value as 'near' — if that value is below EPS_HIT, MIN_FAR_HIT gates on targets an average random start already hits. The pre-edit strict code made this case fail loud (far stratum empty -> far_hit None -> nav_ok False -> NAVIGATION_FAILURE); the edit converted a fail-loud edge case into a fail-silent false-PASS path. remoteness_bands are reported in JSON but nothing in evaluate_gates() consumes them, so the machine verdict — the binding product — is PASS.

5. Nothing in the preregistration handles this. PREREG-PHASE1 s.13 / PREREG-INSTRUMENT s.9 'attainability' checks cover sampling SEs and ceilings, not the per-substrate start-adjacency chance level (which cannot be known pre-run). N1 is called a 'floor baseline' in PREREG-INSTRUMENT s.7 but no gate compares against it. NAV-2 first-passage is reported, never gated. The synthetic control suite contains no tight-ball/start-adjacent pathology (C3's own near/mid triviality is present and unflagged; C3 was caught by the privilege gates, not navigation), so instrument validation provides zero coverage of this failure mode.

Consequence for the binding run: a real substrate whose viable space passes G1 diversity (pkey classes are exact fingerprint identity; hundreds of classes can coexist inside a d1 ball of radius ~0.1, plausible for these VMs where short outputs agree on sentinel padding) but is d1-degenerate would pass G4 pooled, G4 far, and G6 with literally zero navigation, and G5/G7/G8 would not fire (adjacency hits are insensitive to menu ablation/reweighting). Primary flag: PASS = ACCESSIBILITY_GEOMETRY_ESTABLISHED, certifying P2 'intrinsically navigable' by construction rather than by measurement. That is a false PASS of exactly the kind the constitution exists to prevent, and after freeze it cannot be repaired. The suggested fixes (stratum-separation gate with degenerate-strata status blocking PASS, gating on navigated hits with start-sample hits excluded or separately reported, N1 floor reported beside the pair) are the right shape and must be preregistered before freeze.

The zone is occupiable: G4 accepts far-stratum baselines down to 0.10, so a substrate whose far-stratum navigation collapses to 0 under removal of one designed op (rel drop 1.0) yields no flag at baselines 0.15-0.20; PREREG-PHASE1 Section 10 explicitly assigns rare corridor ops to the ablation arm ('rare corridor ops are caught by ablation'), so the identifiability-anisotropy arm does not cover this case, and the synthetic validation never exercised the zone (C3 fired at high baseline, z=6.5). verified.title: Oracle reachability is partially true by construction: target-generating walk edges live in the oracle graph as phenotype-level edges
verified.claim: select_targets records every walk transition into the SAME EdgeStore the oracle BFS consumes, so every target carries its own generating path; edges are stored at pkey level, so a genotype-specific transition becomes 'usable' from ANY genome sharing the parent phenotype. If real-substrate ab-initio starts concentrate on few phenotype classes (likely for total-decode VMs, unlike the uniform-start controls), most episode starts will share a pkey with some generating-walk path and oracle far-reach >= ORACLE_FAR_MIN=0.20 becomes near-automatic — G3 can then never fire and every substrate failure is attributed to NAVIGATION_FAILURE (search weakness) instead of ACCESSIBILITY_FRAGMENTED (topology).
verified.evidence: pipeline.py passes the main `store` to select_targets; metrics.select_targets calls store.edge(sub, f, op, fc) on every walk attempt; oracle_reachability builds radj from store.edges (pkey pairs) and counts an episode reachable iff its start_pkey is in the reverse basin — the basin always contains each target's own generating trajectory back to a random-viable start drawn from the same ab-initio distribution as navigation starts. The v3 'per-episode' repair only helps when start pkeys are diverse (true in the controls, where every node is a distinct pkey and starts are uniform; unverified and implausible for concentrated VM phenotype distributions). Both resulting labels are fatal, so PASS is not inflated — but the topology-vs-search attribution, which is the oracle's entire stated purpose (PREREG-PHASE1 Section 7), is unreliable, and it steers what the next generation concludes about the substrate.
verified.suggested_fix: Report oracle reach twice: with and without target_generation-component edges (tag edges by meter component in EdgeStore), and disclose the phenotype-level aggregation caveat next to any G3/G4 attribution; optionally require basin edges to have been observed from >= 2 distinct parent genomes before they count.
verified.verify_reasoning:
Every mechanical assertion in the claim checks out against the code, and the one unverified premise (start-pkey concentration) is exactly the parameter the design neither measures nor can resolve post-freeze.

VERIFIED MECHANICS (all TRUE as stated):
1. F:/prometheus/agent_d4_blind/d4core/pipeline.py passes the MAIN `store` to select_targets ("tsel = select_targets(sub, rng, ..., store)"); only counterfactual runs get separate cf_store EdgeStores.
2. F:/prometheus/agent_d4_blind/d4core/metrics.py select_targets calls store.edge(sub, f, op, fc) on EVERY walk attempt (before the viability check), so each target's full generating trajectory — back to a rejection-sampled random-viable start — is in store.edges.
3. F:/prometheus/agent_d4_blind/d4core/navigators.py EdgeStore.edge stores bare (pkey_from, pkey_to) tuples: no component tag, no genome provenance, no counts. A genotype-specific transition is therefore treated by the oracle as available from any genome sharing the parent phenotype.
4. F:/prometheus/agent_d4_blind/d4core/oracle.py builds radj from store.edges and counts an episode reachable iff its start_pkey is in the reverse basin of the target's hit-ball. The target's own pkey is in its ball (d1(t,t)=0), so every pkey on the generating-walk prefix is always in the basin.
5. Navigation starts (_sample_viable_start) and target-gen walk starts use the identical rejection-sampling ab-initio distribution.
6. F:/prometheus/agent_d4_blind/d4core/gates.py: G3 fires only if nav fails AND oracle far reach < ORACLE_FAR_MIN (0.20); otherwise G4 appends NAVIGATION_FAILURE. Both labels are fatal — PASS is not inflated, exactly as the reviewer concedes.
7. F:/prometheus/agent_d4_blind/d4core/synthetic.py: in ALL seven validation controls, pkey = node id and random_genome is uniform over n_start distinct nodes, so start-pkey diversity holds BY CONSTRUCTION in every control. The instrument validation (synthetic_control_results.json: C1 and C4 correctly fired ACCESSIBILITY_FRAGMENTED) structurally cannot probe the concentrated-start regime; the v3 per-episode repair was only ever demonstrated where "its own start" is a distinct pkey.

WHY THIS IS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT ALREADY HANDLED:
- The mechanism is a residual hole in the v3 repair the amendment log claims to have closed: under pkey concentration, "its own start" collapses back into "some walk's start" at phenotype resolution. The generating path in the basin is a selected trajectory (the walk DEFINED the target as its own endpoint), so episode reachability via start-pkey collision with the generating walk is uninformative about whether a pre-specified far target is findable from that start class — probability ≈ concentration, independent of topology. Additionally, the op-census web (1,200 parents drawn from the same ab-initio pool × 20 transitions) densely interconnects common pkeys, so a single collision anywhere on any prefix suffices; far reach ≥ 0.20 plausibly becomes near-automatic once top-pkey mass is ~0.2-0.3.
- PREREG-PHASE1 Section 7 states the oracle's ENTIRE purpose is topology-vs-search attribution, and Section 13 requires every gate value be checked for attainability before freeze; ORACLE_FAR_MIN's fireability on real substrates depends on an unmeasured concentration parameter (this mirrors the user's own feedback_gate_must_be_shown_reachable doctrine, in reverse: G3 may be ineligible to fire on any input). The "topological ceiling" language handles the direction of bias for the G3 side (low ceiling → sound fragmentation claim) but nothing discloses the pkey-aggregation caveat or the guaranteed presence of each target's generating path.

The encoding facts are accurately reported, but the claim's defect framing fails on three grounds: the preregistration explicitly routes this channel to a dedicated assay, the "invisible corridor" characterization mislabels intended channel separation as a blind spot, and the residual weakness it leans on is a separate, already-filed finding rather than an independent defect.

VERIFIED FACTS (F:/prometheus/agent_d4_blind/substrates/vm_substrates.py): S1 op=(w>>12)&0xF with IN=12 (1100), OUT=13 (1101) at lines 285-293; S2 op=(b>>5)&7 with IN=6, OUT=7 at lines 389-400; S4 op=byte&7 with IN=4, OUT=5 at lines 505-513. All three pairs are Hamming distance 1; a single OP0 bitflip (hi-byte bit 4 in S1, byte bit 5 in S2, byte bit 0 in S4) interconverts IN and OUT. Also correct: PRIV-1 labels are menu-operator indices (d4core/classifier.py; feats/rows_op in d4core/metrics.py op_census), the ablation loop removes only menu operators (d4core/pipeline.py lines 124-137), and PRIV-2 is a covariance eigenshare of the displacement cloud (metrics.py lines 152-157). And IN/OUT are genuinely the two viability-critical instruction classes (viability requires nonempty output AND input sensitivity, both reachable only through IN and OUT).

WHY THIS IS NOT A DEFECT AS STATED:

1. The preregistration already assigns this exact channel to PRIV-4. PREREG-INSTRUMENT.md Section 2 defines four assays as covering four DISTINCT designer channels and says so explicitly: "(d) through the binary coding itself (PRIV-4). These are the channels the designer actually controls once physics is fixed." That PRIV-1/2/3 cannot attribute an encoding-adjacency effect is the design, not a hole — PRIV-1 targets menu partitioning, PRIV-3 targets load-bearing menu primitives, PRIV-2 targets induced geometry. The claim itself concedes PRIV-4 is the assay for this channel. And PRIV-4's perturbation is exactly on target: ENC_PERM (vm_substrates.py lines 47-48, applied in _decode_byte line 92-93) randomizes the byte-value-to-opcode preimage, so single-bit raw flips no longer preferentially interconvert IN and OUT — OP0 does not commute with the re-coding while cell-level OP1-OP4 do, which is precisely the disclosed point of the counterfactual (file docstring lines 17-20, PREREG-PHASE1 Section 8).

2. "Designed corridor" overstates what a dense total-decode code can avoid. In a dense n-bit opcode field every opcode is Hamming-1 from log2(N) others; S1's OUT is equally one flip from HLT and SKZ, and IN one flip from SWAP and MOV — adjacencies the claim does not flag, though OUT->HLT is at least as behavior-determining. Under a uniformly random opcode assignment (the reviewer's own primary fix), IN/OUT land at Hamming-1 with probability 3/7 (~43%) in each 3-bit substrate and 4/15 (~27%) in S1 — the proposed randomization would reproduce the flagged property nearly half the time in S2/S4, which shows adjacency per se is generic dense-code texture, not a distinctive designer thumbprint. Only ~5% joint probability for all three, which is worth a disclosure sentence but is not evidence of a load-bearing highway.

3. "Load-bearing" is conjecture, and the instrument that would decide it is not blind to it. G7 compares baseline navigation against the ENC_PERM variant with fresh targets generated under the re-coded physics (pipeline.py lines 185-210; gates.py lines 175-184). The self-matched-targets design partially cancels kernel effects, but not fully — C6_CHAOS generated targets under its own physics and still failed navigation (synthetic_control_results.json), so G7's statistic does move when kernel quality degrades. If destroying the adjacency degrades navigability, G7 can fire; if it does not fire (and runs), the corridor was not disproportionately responsible for practical accessibility under the prereg's own operational definition of privilege, and the PASS is honest.

4. The constitution has a second preregistered catch for exactly this object. PREREG-PHASE1 Section 11 (human-taxonomy red team) allows recognizable edit-family classifications — an IN<->OUT single-bit interconversion family is the paradigm case of "cheap edits corresponding to designed semantics" — to be applied post-run and to DOWNGRADE a PASS to PRIVILEGED_CORRIDOR. So even a corridor missed by all four PRIV assays does not escape the verdict machinery after freeze; the one-sidedness (weaken only) is exactly the charter rule.

5. The claim's only real teeth are borrowed from a separate finding. Its funnel argument depends entirely on "PRIV-4/G7 is precisely the assay shown above to be skippable and confounded" — referencing a previously-filed defect. I verified that skip path exists (pipeline.py lines 209-210 set representation status non-OK on POOL_TOO_SMALL; gates.py line 176 then never evaluates G7), and it should be fixed under THAT finding (the claim's own minimum fix is "make G7 unskippable — previous finding"). Once G7 is unskippable, this claim reduces to: a disclosed-channel encoding feature, covered by the assay built for it, with a post-run red-team downgrade as backstop. That is the prereg working as designed, not a missed defect. Adding a Hamming->=2 opcode-separation counterfactual would be extra robustness, but its absence does not invalidate the binding run given PRIV-4 + Section 11 cover the channel.

The failure scenario is real and uncovered by any other gate. A physics whose operators all funnel non-identity change into a few destination phenotype classes (e.g. echo/collapse attractors, entirely plausible in these total-decode VMs): G2 passes (transitions are non-identity, children viable, all ops alive); PRIV-1 sits near chance (no operator owns the funnel, so the joint acc>0.30 AND aniso>0.75 trigger cannot fire — and with several hubs the displacement cloud is multi-directional, keeping aniso low anyway); PRIV-3 ablation shows no collapse (the funnel is shared across ops); G7/G8 are insensitive (the funnel lives in decode/dynamics, not the menu or byte coding). minor_unverified.evidence: metrics.op_census: 1,200 parents x 5 ops x 4 reps; s.13 acknowledges clustering by parent for the classifier split but the G2 SE quote does not cluster.
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Re-quote G2 SEs from a parent-level bootstrap (resample parents) and report that CI beside the verdict.

minor_unverified.title: Oracle episode attribution biased toward ACCESSIBILITY_FRAGMENTED: only first start recorded, N4 crossover paths invisible
minor_unverified.claim: Episode oracle-reachability tests only the episode's FIRST viable start pkey against the basin, but N1/N2/N3 episodes restart from many fresh starts mid-run and N4 holds up to 16 population members — an episode whose later restart or other population member lay in the basin is scored unreachable. Additionally N4's actual hit paths can traverse crossover edges that are excluded from the oracle graph. Both biases underestimate episode reach, pushing ofar below ORACLE_FAR_MIN and shifting failure attribution from NAVIGATION_FAILURE toward ACCESSIBILITY_FRAGMENTED. Both labels are fatal, so no verdict flips, but the attribution narrative (topology vs search weakness) — the oracle's sole purpose — is biased in a known direction.
minor_unverified.evidence: navigators.py: start_pkey set once at the first viable start (n1/n2/n3) and at the first viable population member (n4); restart starts update g/f but never start_pkey. oracle.py uses r['start_pkey'] only. Crossover exclusion is the disclosed v2 repair, but its interaction with per-episode attribution for N4 episodes is not disclosed.
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Record all episode start pkeys (list) and score an episode reachable if ANY of its own starts lies in the basin; disclose in the verdict that N4 episode attribution excludes crossover moves.

minor_unverified.title: Planned per-stratum n not enforced; tie-degenerate strata can silently stop measuring remoteness
minor_unverified.claim: select_targets only rejects pools smaller than 3*(k_low+k_high)=24, so a decile stratum of a small pool can hold 2-3 targets and the far gate then runs at n=10-15 runs instead of the prereg's quoted n=40, with no minimum-stratum guard and no disclosure. The mid-audit edit (inclusive bands >= q[1] / >= q[3] plus global dedup) prevents empty strata under ties, but under a heavily tied remoteness distribution (q[0]==q[3]) it fills 'far' with targets at the SAME remoteness as 'near' — the far gate then measures nothing about remoteness while still reporting a 'far' hit rate against MIN_FAR_HIT.
minor_unverified.evidence: metrics.py select_targets: POOL_TOO_SMALL check `len(pool_items) < 3 * (k_low + k_high)`; chosen = all of by_dens when len < k_low+k_high; new inclusive masks with chosen_global dedup (uncommitted edit, comment 'inclusive bands + global dedup').
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Record realized stratum sizes and the remoteness spread q[3]-q[0] in target_selection output; prereg a floor (e.g. >= 4 targets per stratum and q[3]-q[0] >= 2/64) below which the far gate is declared unevaluable rather than silently evaluated on a degenerate stratum.

minor_unverified.title: Winner's-curse selection: far-hit and refind gates evaluated only on the post-hoc best pooled navigator
minor_unverified.claim: best_pair_nav is chosen as the max of two pooled hit rates, then its far-stratum rate and refind ratio are the gated quantities. Selection by pooled maximum biases the selected navigator's statistics upward (favoring PASS on G4-far/G6), and the far gate is judged on a navigator selected by a different criterion — N2 could win pooled while N4 is the only navigator that reaches far targets, failing the substrate on the wrong navigator's far rate. With only two candidates the bias is modest but nonzero and one-directional per gate.
minor_unverified.evidence: metrics.py summarize_navigation best_pair_nav = argmax pooled_hit_rate; gates.py far_hit and refind read best_stats only.
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Gate far-hit on the max far rate across the competitive pair (prereg that choice), or report both navigators' far/refind with CIs beside the verdict and prereg which one binds.

minor_unverified.title: Oracle per-episode attribution uses only the first viable start; restart and fresh-injection starts are invisible
minor_unverified.claim: An episode is judged oracle-reachable iff its recorded start_pkey lies in the basin (oracle.py:32-33, 48-50), but N1/N2/N3 resample fresh ab-initio starts on every restart (nonviable_restart=25 within a 1200-eval budget yields many restarts) and N4 injects fresh genomes at p_fresh=0.05 throughout; none of those starts update the row's start_pkey (navigators.py:105-112, 171-178, 228-233, 291-295). The 'its OWN start lies in the basin' criterion therefore understates each episode's real start set, biasing episode-reach downward and pushing failed navigation from NAVIGATION_FAILURE toward ACCESSIBILITY_FRAGMENTED. Attribution-level only (both flags are fatal, PASS/FAIL unaffected), and it partially offsets in the opposite direction of the viability-ball defect, making the G3 number a mix of two opposing biases.
minor_unverified.evidence: navigators.py: start_pkey set once per run (lines 75-77, 137-139, 206-208, 275-278) and never updated on restart; oracle.py:48-50 counts membership of that single pkey. RunResult carries no restart-start list.
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Record every fresh ab-initio start pkey of the episode in the run row (list), and count the episode oracle-reachable iff any of its starts lies in the basin; disclose the definition in PREREG-PHASE1 Section 7 before freeze.

minor_unverified.title: Encoding counterfactual's target generation is metered to the baseline 'target_generation' component
minor_unverified.claim: select_targets unconditionally calls sub.meter.set_component('target_generation') (metrics.py:239). In the representation counterfactual the pipeline sets the component to 'counterfactual' (pipeline.py:192) and then calls select_targets on the encoded substrate, which silently re-labels the component, so all encoded-variant target-generation evaluations (~48 walks x 150 steps x up to 5 attempts on a real run) are booked to the baseline 'target_generation' meter bucket. Budgets bind on loop counters so no run length changes, but the preregistered per-component meter disclosure (PREREG-PHASE1 Section 9 'Every evaluate() metered per component'; anti_cheat.json structural guarantee) is wrong for every real-substrate results.json.
minor_unverified.evidence: metrics.py:239; pipeline.py encoded block (meter.set_component('counterfactual') at line ~192 immediately followed by select_targets at ~194-196, which resets the component). Synthetic runs never hit this path (is_real=False), so the recorded control meters look clean.
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Give select_targets a component parameter defaulting to 'target_generation' and pass 'counterfactual' from the encoding block (or save/restore meter.component around the call).

minor_unverified.title: Anti-cheat static check scope gap: oracle isolation enforced only by pipeline ordering, pipeline/oracle/classifier files unscanned, unseeded numpy randomness unchecked
minor_unverified.claim: FORBIDDEN (static_checks.py:39-52) scans only navigators.py, interface.py, vm_substrates.py, and metrics.py. d4core/pipeline.py — the one file that actually routes oracle output — plus oracle.py, classifier.py, synthetic.py, and run_phase1.py are never scanned, so a future edit feeding oracle output into select_targets or run_navigation would keep anti_cheat.json 'clean: true'. The vm_substrates pattern list omits os./sys. (the special header-strip at lines 91-93 implies they were intended), so e.g. os.environ entering substrate state would pass. The MANIFEST claim 'All machine-visible information is enumerated in anti_cheat/' is currently true by manual inspection (I verified the pipeline ordering: oracle_reachability runs after all navigation and its output reaches only evaluate_gates), but the static certificate covers less than it implies and the gap survives the freeze.

minor_unverified.title: The machine-readable instrument-validity bit is stripped from the validation artifact by _san

minor_unverified.title: Instrument validated at DEFAULT_CFG scale, binding runs use REAL_CFG scale
minor_unverified.claim: validate_instrument.py calls run_pipeline(sub, {}, ...) so all seven controls were classified under DEFAULT_CFG (census 4000, 800 op-parents, 18 targets from k=3+3, nav budget 800), while the binding runs use REAL_CFG (census 10000, 1200 parents, 24 targets from k=4+4, budget 1200) — confirmed by the control meters (census 4000, operator_census 16400). Thresholds are shared, but the power and target-suite geometry of the assays the thresholds were calibrated against differ from the binding configuration, so PREREG-PHASE1 Section 12's 'the binding instrument is the one that classifies all seven controls correctly' holds only at the calibration scale, and the SE-at-gate numbers quoted in Section 10 (e.g. n=120, n=40) were never exercised on a control.

minor_unverified.title: Reversibility census samples only the earliest parents (rev_pool caps at the first 1600 non-identity transitions)
minor_unverified.claim: rev_pool stops accepting candidates at rev_sample*4 = 1600 entries (metrics.py:74-75), which on a substrate with a healthy effective rate fills within the first ~100 of 1200 parents; the fixed-seed permutation (default_rng(9900), line 108) then shuffles only within this early-parent pool. Reversibility is therefore measured over the earliest census parents rather than the parent population, a wrong-population statistic. It is report-only (never gated), so severity is minor, but it ships in the frozen results as a per-operator number.
minor_unverified.evidence: metrics.py:74-75 (cap during the parent loop), :108 (permutation within the capped pool). With effective rate ~0.5 and 20 transitions per parent, 1600 candidates accrue by parent ~160 of 1200.
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Reservoir-sample rev_pool across all parents (seeded), or collect all non-identity transitions' (parent-index, rep) keys and subsample after the loop with default_rng(9900).

minor_unverified.title: Remoteness-spike strata degeneracy: mid stratum can silently vanish and no minimum per-stratum target/run count is enforced
minor_unverified.claim: Strata are relative quantiles of the pool's remoteness. When the remoteness distribution is a spike (hub-dominated pool), quantile ties make q[1] == q[2] and the mid mask (remoteness > q[1]) & (remoteness <= q[2]) is empty; near (<= q[0]) can absorb far more than a decile via ties. select_targets also returns fewer than k_low+k_high members per stratum without complaint (len(by_dens) < k_low + k_high branch), and POOL_TOO_SMALL only fires below 3*(k_low+k_high) = 24 pool members. Nothing downstream checks target counts: PREREG-PHASE1 promises '24 targets total' and quotes gate SEs at n=120/40, but gates.py evaluates G4's far gate on whatever runs exist — conceivably 1 far target x 5 seeds — and pooled-hit denominators shift silently. The full-spike case (no far stratum) correctly fails via far_hit None, but partial degeneracy passes with unreported n collapse.
minor_unverified.evidence: metrics.py lines 289-303 (quantile masks, chosen truncation); gates.py lines 116-123 (no n checks; far_hit read from whatever stratum rows exist); PREREG-PHASE1 sections 5 and 10 (24 targets; n=120/40 SE claims).
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Add to select_targets a hard status (STRATA_DEGENERATE) when any stratum yields fewer than k_low+k_high members or when remoteness bands collide (q[0]==q[3]), and make gates treat that status as a primary failure (poverty/scale flag). Record per-stratum n in margins and refuse gate evaluation below the preregistered n.

minor_unverified.title: Oracle basin includes non-viable phenotypes navigators can never score as hits, biasing failure attribution toward NAVIGATION_FAILURE
minor_unverified.claim: The hit ball is built from ALL stored phenotypes ('ball = [pk for pk, f in all_pkeys if sub.d1(f, tfp) <= eps_hit]') with no viability filter, and the edge store records parent->child edges even when the child is non-viable. Every navigator, however, checks the hit condition only inside 'if sub.viable(fc)', so a non-viable phenotype inside the ball is oracle-reachable but constitutionally unhittable, and paths terminating in non-viable ball members inflate basin size. Effect: episodes get classified 'oracle-reachable but M0-missed' (search weakness / NAVIGATION_FAILURE) when the topology available to viability-respecting search actually had no path (ACCESSIBILITY_FRAGMENTED). Both flags are fatal so PASS is unaffected, but the P2-vs-substrate attribution the oracle exists to provide — and the G3 gate that consumes strata_reach — is skewed in a fixed direction.
minor_unverified.evidence: oracle.py lines 37-47 (no viable() filter on ball or basin membership); navigators.py: hit checks nested under sub.viable(fc) in n1 (lines 92-99), n2 (153-158), n3 (225-242), n4 (306-310); metrics.py op_census/select_targets record edges to non-viable children via store.edge before viability checks.
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Filter ball membership to viable phenotypes (hits require viable(fc)) and either drop edges whose child is non-viable from the oracle graph or keep them only when the child later appears as a parent. Re-validate C1/C4/C6 attribution after the change.

minor_unverified.title: G1's 250-class diversity floor is counted on a finer equivalence than the geometry navigation is tested on
minor_unverified.claim: pkey hashes (outputs, steps bucket, touched bucket, halted) per probe, while d1 — the sole distance used for targets, hits, remoteness, and density — sees outputs only. Two phenotypes with identical outputs on all probes but different step/touched buckets are distinct G1 classes at d1 = 0. The MIN_CLASSES = 250 floor can therefore be met entirely by bucket-jitter classes that are behaviorally indistinguishable to every downstream measurement, so 'viable behavioral diversity' (P1) is certified on an axis navigation never traverses. This is one of the charter's named collapse risks (diversity standing in for another coordinate) and it composes with the hub finding: a hub substrate's G1 pass is partly bucket jitter.
minor_unverified.evidence: vm_substrates.py ProbeFingerprint._key line 69 (includes r[1], r[2], r[3]); d1 lines 176-187 (outputs only); gates.py MIN_CLASSES 250 reads census n_classes_viable which counts pkey classes (metrics.py run_census lines 26-32).
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Report both counts (pkey classes and output-distinct classes, i.e. classes under the d1=0 quotient) and gate G1 on the output-distinct count, or disclose in PREREG-PHASE1 that the diversity floor includes resource-profile-only distinctions and add a margin entry showing the output-distinct number beside it.

minor_unverified.title: Doc/code drift bundle to reconcile before freeze (witness flag, viability docstring, C3 gateway share, G7/G8 z-condition, target-gen seed independence, validation-vs-binding config n's)
minor_unverified.claim: Five documented properties diverge from the code that will be hashed: (1) run_phase1.py labels a non-viable expressivity witness as PHENOTYPE_POVERTY — the vocabulary has no expressivity flag, conflating P0 failure with P1 failure. (2) vm_substrates.py header and PREREG-PHASE1 section 2 promise '>= 1 executed state-changing step', but viable() tests any(r[1] > 0) where steps counts every executed instruction, making the clause vacuous for S1/S2/S4 (steps >= 1 always); only S3 implements the stated semantics (rewrite count) — and this clause is the only thing excluding S3 pure-echo, so its semantics are load-bearing. (3) PREREG-INSTRUMENT section 5 says C3's corridor crosses 'from a 1% gateway subset'; code gateway is cx >= 48, i.e. 2 of 50 columns = 4% of cluster A. (4) The just-added z >= 1.96 condition on G7/G8 in gates.py appears nowhere in PREREG-PHASE1 section 10, whose text still reads as pure band tests. (5) PREREG-INSTRUMENT section 6 says targets are generated 'with its own seed', and anti_cheat.json claims an 'independent seed family', but select_targets consumes the same continuous rng stream as the census (pipeline.py passes the one generator through) — independent of navigation's hash-derived seeds, yes, but not a separate seed family from census. Additionally the validation runs used DEFAULT_CFG (census 4000, 18 targets, budget 800, op_parents 800) while the binding run uses REAL_CFG (10000, 24, 1200, 1200), so all calibration margins were measured at different n than the SE claims quoted in section 10.
minor_unverified.evidence: run_phase1.py lines 60-66; vm_substrates.py lines 157-165 vs header line 11 and S3 lines 441-459; synthetic.py C3 lines 171-175 vs PREREG-INSTRUMENT section 5; gates.py G7/G8 blocks (z_gate ABLATION_MIN_Z) vs PREREG-PHASE1 section 10 G7/G8 text; pipeline.py lines 79-101 (single rng for census + targets) vs anti_cheat.json structural_guarantees; validate_instrument.py line 26 run_pipeline(sub, {}, ...) = DEFAULT_CFG vs REAL_CFG in run_phase1.py.
minor_unverified.suggested_fix: Reconcile each pair textually before hashing: add an EXPRESSIVITY_FAILURE flag (or rename the note), fix viable() to count state-changing steps or amend the docstring/prereg, correct the C3 gateway figure, write the G7/G8 z-condition into section 10, either give select_targets its own seeded generator or amend the seed-independence claims, and add a disclosure that instrument calibration ran at DEFAULT_CFG n's with the margin implications stated.
